script.summary: A script to check the XML files in this repository for XML well-formedness, counting Chinese characters and English words in XML files, generating a summary report.
script.usage: python projectdir/scripts/check_xml.py [path] [path] can be a directory or a single XML file. If [path] is omitted, the script will check all XML files in the repository.
script.example: python projectdir/scripts/check_xml.py python projectdir/scripts/check_xml.py faiths python projectdir/scripts/check_xml.py faiths/faran.xml

script.summary: A script to package all the XML document files into a single XML file, which can be used for distribution purposes. The script will resolve all XInclude references and generate a single XML file containing all the XML textual content of the repository. Additional files still need to be included manually, such as images and other non-XML files.
script.usage:
python projectdir/scripts/package.py [output_file] [output_file] is the name of the output XML file. If omitted, the default name is "rakia-verse-package.xml".
If the option "--no-emit" is specified, the script will only perform parsing and validation, and will not write the output file.

script.summary: A script to convert dates between the Kingdom Calendar (KC/BK, 360 days per year, 15 months of 24 days) and the Hijri Calendar (AH/BH, 343 days per year, 7 months of 49 days). The epoch anchor is 0001-01-01AH = 1372-08-23BK. Neither calendar has a year 0.
script.usage:
python projectdir/scripts/calendar_convert.py [date ...] [date] can be a full date like "1372-08-23BK" or "0001-01-01AH" for exact conversion, or a bare year like "618BK" to get the corresponding year range. Multiple dates can be given at once.
If no argument is given, the script enters interactive stdio mode, reading one date per line ("q" to quit).
script.example: python projectdir/scripts/calendar_convert.py 1372-08-23BK python projectdir/scripts/calendar_convert.py 618BK 0325KC python projectdir/scripts/calendar_convert.py

script.summary: A helper script to scale the two map images in the repository to 1.5x their original size, using nearest neighbor resampling for the border map and Lanczos resampling for the main map.

A script to calculate the distance between two hexagonal grid cells in an odd-r offset coordinate system (pointy-top orientation). The script outputs both grid distance and actual physical distance in kilometers based on the hex side length (default 40km, yielding a center-to-center spacing of ~69.28km).
script.usage:
python projectdir/scripts/hex_distance.py col1 row1 col2 row2 [-s HEX_SIDE] [-v]
col1, row1: The column and row coordinates of the first cell. col2, row2: The column and row coordinates of the second cell. -s, --hex-side: The side length of the hexagon in kilometers (default: 40). -v, --verbose: Display detailed information including cube coordinates.
script.example: python projectdir/scripts/hex_distance.py 0 0 3 2 python projectdir/scripts/hex_distance.py 0 0 3 2 -v python projectdir/scripts/hex_distance.py 0 0 1 0 -s 20
